item.title: Title
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
Usually, people don't care about whose number they save in their contacts list. Some do, maybe because they have their privacy set to "My Contact List" on their WhatsApp, or because they don't save someone's number simply because they're a piece of shit. (The subject in the previous sentence can either be taken as the former, or the latter. Your choice).

Weirdly enough, people wonder how their friend-person save their names. They look for emojis, nicknames, or an unflattering picture as the contact picture. This, to my (silly, foolish,) morally superior mind, seems unnecessary.

Nicknames. Having one of those is not a fucking trophy, it is not a thing that is meant to be used just to seem cool among peers. It is almost as bad as writing tl;dr stuff as Birthday greetings for someone on absolutely every social media site imaginable but to their faces. (Wait, what?)

If the image above is not relatable enough, try this:

 

Address your loved ones using any name you like (or don't even use a name, just go for expletives). Save pictures for their name however you like (or don't). Make sure they have a happy birthday.

Just don't do this type of shit while a weird guy who'd post about you having a good life on an *apparently* pretentious blog that has a word count that shouldn't even be called pretentious by law like it is a bad thing, is around. He's probably doing it just to seem cool.

(Or don't, I'm not your mom.) (Or am I?)

item.title: home?
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
To live in a house at a city, sometimes in a multi-story apartment, with a lovely family that has every little shit needed within reach- groceries, clothing, gym, pools, games, internet and all things considered necessary in this millennium, is pretty much every person's dream. But not mine.

Not to be completely secluded from human existence though, I'm not one of those who sport a Bob Marley T-shirt without knowing who the fuck he is and blast "One Love, One Life" like it is some kind of an anthem and claim that the hippy life is the best, but I'd like to be relatively secluded from the busy-ness that life tries to impose on us.

This being a pretentious blog (apparently) and I (the author, lol), who considers to be a Woke™ individual to an extent, like to live in solidarity. Not like a caveman though, with all things necessary for living. With nice food, a select bunch of loved ones, a pet, a pool, books, internet (I need my daily dose of memes! Don't judge me!).

I'm not saying that I will live like that; I just like the idea of it. I might realize this dream, or I won't. Just don't screenshot this and show this to my face if I never do this. Pls.

Imagine a cup of coffee, a comfortable sofa beside the window and you're sitting on it, watching the cool droplets of water drip over the leaves and join the rest of the pool caused by the rain at a lazy Sunday morning. A kid, pet dog and a spouse would be even better. Like an icing on a cake. Cat's meow. Bees Knees. Beyond reproach. Top of the line. (What? Do I need to stop with the idioms? No I won't! You're not my mom!)

Or are you?

etbjnee

item.title: what's fair
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
Lets face it, this whole "life" thing is a disaster. It has always been one. There is "Fair Treatment" on unnecessary things, and hardly anything is fair in the shit that needs to be. Both an IIT graduate and a local graduate can be engineers. They have to be seen at the same level when it is in a paper.

But in reality, its different. I probably can't do anything that an IIT graduate does. (Who cares, I'm still a graduate!). But they get the upper hand at interviews, get the jobs they deserve, live the life they've earned. But it doesn't mean that students from other universities won't be successful. They could get better in time. Or do something else, like writing (whaaaa!), art, film making, photography, etc. There are many examples for that. (That's right! I don't need the course I spent a shit ton of money and time to be successful in life! Take that, high school teacher who said that I'd be worthless!)

But how does one live just by doing those art-y shit? Over the time, many people who were successful creators of art reached their statuses and proved to be an inspiration for masses. It is a simple but complicated concept: being oneself. (Wow, oxymoron much?)

It's actually easy to be yourself. It doesn't mean that I should put myself in the top of the priority list (although, that'd be nice),  but do things in our own style. And there's where things get tricky: One's own Style.

How does one find their own, original style? The answer, I guess, is we don't. My reasoning is that, there is no style that is original. Let's take music for example, if we break it down, it is a compilation of sounds, arranged within bars and scales to make it different from random noises. Any sound needs some basic requirements to prove to be called Music. One needs to find a way to make it seem new. But in essence, it is simply an iteration of musical notes that happened to come out of someone specific.

Plagiarism still needs to be condemned. Theft of intellectual property is a thing. That is something we need to have in our minds.

I started to post vague pictures in Instagram that mildly resembled the situations and conditions I put myself into, and I found it to be the most emotionally revealing shit I've done in my life. (@actualjoel, if you want to see the weird shit I share there). Then I saw one of my friends post a blog in here. She is very good in writing, and the things she wrote inspired me to try it. I never had any idea about what to write, but then I decided to extend the shit I post on Instagram with a bunch of words.

And I guess that's how creativity works; you take one thing and merge with another and it seems new.

What's fair is that, we are given equally levelled pedestals to step into life, and where we reach is up to us.

Well, pardon me for the lack of pictures and the usual pathetic attempts at humor, my mom asked me to tone it down. Also, no idioms today.

etbjnee.

item.title: regret
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
(If you thought that I wouldn't use that picture as the featured image, well, you were wrong. I hope you ragret your mistake).

There is no point in brooding over past. But there is no point in being logical all the time either. That's why I constantly think about all those weird shit I managed to do and hope I'd rather die than being in a similar situation again. What an awesome concept are these "thoughts"?  I hope the person who created these "thoughts" choke on his food to death.

I regret wanting to be a doctor. It made me choose Biology as one of the papers at High School, and end up getting good marks only in that fucking subject. My love for that subject made my Physics teacher hate every person who took biology. And here I am, starting my masters' course in a few days, that has nothing to do with Biology, and everything to do with Physics. Brilliant.

 

There's many small instances of self- disgust I feel that doesn't require much words to explain, like standing in front of the line just to seem good to my teacher, agreeing to be the house captain for sports day without knowing jack shit about the games we're about to play, eating too much Biriyani and receiving the poop lord's blessing as a consequence, being born in general, etc.,

 

A silly buddy problem caused quite a ruffle at school when I was 13. The class teacher, as a result, came into the conclusion that I'm a problematic child. Her vocal wars on me were fun. Funny thing is, she is the only one who thought that I'm a bad person. Many teachers would say that I was the most quiet person in the class. (HA! better regret your mistake, you bad, bad lady!)

Truth is, I'm neither quiet, nor problematic. I used to be a person who talk to people only when I need something. It is only when I turned 20, I have realized this thing about me. There was some kind of stupid justification, but it never made sense. I was opportunistic, that's what most people's perception about me is. As a result, I ramble about all kinds of shit in the internet instead of doing it to a friend. (This is not a pity parade though, just one of my regrets). I managed to make friends now, and they're fine. So, sorry to that one girl who was a dear friend of mine with whom I stopped talking, just because we were in different classes when were 10. I was a stupid boi and a bad friend. (I'm still stupid though, but that's a different blog). 

There's a lot more friendships lost in the same way though, but this is the one I happen to regret the most.

There's no way I could turn those conclusions around, so it's better to work on not being as stupid as I was, in the future.     etbjnee.

item.title: trends
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
It was 2013. everything was very odd.

I was a naive kid, who had no idea what a mey-mey is. But then, the MEEM Nation attacked. The "What is that picture? Why are my friends sharing this? Is this supposed to be funny? This is what they do?" phase slowly transitioned into "Hey dude, this is sooo DANKE"  within months. By then, I began using rage comics ironically (I know, I'm very late to the party) within my friend group.

They are not too funny, it never were. But I think it's the context and the inside joke thing we have with our friends along with some weird thrill that is felt while sharing our conversation out in the public (at least within our friends who weren't a part of that particular conversation).

But, there are few things that are more opportunistic than a YouTube video that says,

"Hey guys, here's a fidget spinner video-" "Here's a funny video that we made that has the exact same format as the other funny video you saw yesterday-" "Here's what this person in BIG BOSS did that was aired on TV but see it here too, because I have added slow motion shots and some grammatically wrong words to it"

I'm not a commodity. I'm not a demographic. There's absolutely no respect to people from me who treat me like that.

There is literally no person in this world who aren't influenced by trends. Clothes, lifestyle, brands, there's a time for everything to shine for a period of time. It's a normal thing in life, and nobody gets to judge it. But exploiting a thing for some kind of a gain is what I find odd. (Clothing trend is fine, I guess. Either I'm a walking hypocrite or a stupid idiot, your choice. My mom said not to care about it anyway!).

"Engineering is the worst course right now!", says the guy who has umpteen arrears and spends most of his time in the gates. Funny thing is, for a guy who sets foot into his classes almost never, there will be an impressive number of "Last Bencher" memes on his Facebook timeline.

"VIP da! VIP da! We sacrifice so much da!"

Usually, it is not the people who are able to work hard complain about the course, it is those who don't. While there are students who do well despite of their low scores, marks are still meant to be a valid requirement.

There's another kind of people, who use terms in their social media accounts simply because it looks cool, and under the impression of "If I use this word, I'm cool". 

"Rider"- Okay, dude who went to a road trip one time a few months ago. "Daddys_Little_Girl"  - Seriously, don't. This has a very different meaning in the internet language. Pls. "She_Calls_Me_Bae" -  and I_calls_you_stupid. Howboudat? 

Its your internet, your life, whatever you use is nobody else's business. But, for the love of god, know what you use.

Here's a picture of me:  Okay, I do it too.  I used the only mom joke in the middle of this post somewhere, so no mom joke here. So here's another overused joke instead- "My life". (LMAO DANKE) etbjnee.

item.title: bad brain
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
I guess every activity we do boils down to one thing- fun.

People follow their passion to satisfy their heart. Once the heart feels content, every little hardship that comes wouldn't seem as much of a problem. If I get to work in a facility that makes prostheses, any research question I could possibly encounter would make me happy, as I get to use the things I know (and going to learn) to make something that could potentially be useful.

People want to be liked, at least to the people they like/ wish to be friends with. I'm no exception. But it is always a whirlwind of emotions when I'm in any kind of a social situation. It usually follows the following thought process:

I can do this, people will like me!I guess?

Okay, now is my chance to shine. I better not fuck this up. Here we go! Okay, I made a little mistake, hope they don't mind this.

Please don't judge me, cool person! Okay, their expression changes. I've officially blew it. Great. Shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit shit Why did I even think this would work? I'm terrible at first impressions. I better say this fact about me, "LOL I'm sorry, I don't do well at  first impressions." There, hope it lightens things up. No it didn't.  Okay, quick, make some lameass statement that eases the situation. -That made this even more uncomfortable. Fine, just blabber something till someone else joins the conversation so that you can show yourself out. *after exiting the convo like a ninja*

Ooh, another potential friend-- -- nah, why bother!

Then its the usual stuff, having an existential crisis at midnight and spending shower time pondering why I exist. You know, no biggie.

I believe everyone has a fun, non judgmental bunch of friends. And it eats me alive when my friends don't talk to me about their problems and make plans without me. I must've did something terrible that took me out of their "good" list. And the good 'ole brain starts a troubleshooting session that over analyses every little thing I did in the past with them starts, and its never fun. I need to be whoever I want (i.e., fun, non judgmental friend), and I've failed to be one.

Its never like the movies or books, right, like how the protagonists in John Green novels always get to hit Emma Watsons and Cara Delevignes. But even in those stuff, there would be an outcast-yet-friendly character we'd like. The thing about them is that they don't seem to give a shit about what seemsto be the important stuff.  They stand out from the rest of the others, that's what makes them likable.

That reminds me of one thing: I've always liked DC Movies (I know). And in a true fanboy fashion, Marvel movies are a no-no for me. No matter the criticisms, I've never stopped liking them, and even went to a point where I no longer look out for reviews for any entertainment thing I find interesting; I check them and rate for myself, and trying to not force my opinions on others.

I think low self- esteem in a person is simply a thought that they need to be better. It is a bit weird to read that sentence, but hear me out, it is our brains way of making us realize how much of a shitty outcome we give out to the world by pointing out every little bad thing we did, offering little to no solutions for that. We should probably need some other source for the solutions, either from within, or by talking to a trusted person.

Just like my adamant movie choices, I should find a way to overcome my (not yet diagnosed) social anxiety and self- esteem problems.

I would,

Probably.

item.title: no assumptions.
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
He's not unique,

He never was.

There were many things he copied to create an illusion of originality.

 

Never original, yet different; a pompous display of being weird.

"Pretentious!", he proclaimed, but hardly did any physical deed that garners attention.

Being vague is all he could do.

 

Mostly serious, but pretended otherwise;

Said "Be yourself!", but chose different things, just to stand out.

To the unaware, he was different.

 

But he knew.

item.title: fun person
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
It was a typical Sunday afternoon. I was going through my usual “Judge everyone who are trying to be pretentious that are not me” time on Quora. You know, the usual. The extra-spicy chicken fry had me extra-active, so I was putting my energy to good use, even though there were a shitload of assignments and term papers to turn in. There were those typical shit, like how the All-Good-Guy was unjustly cheated by his then teenage love and how he turned it into a life changing story. Then there was this nice lady that stood up for a child treated badly by the shopping-crazed mother. Oh, and there was this hilariously funny comedic events that occurred to this person at a bus, written with such wit and humour, that it can be printed on a paper and a shooting for a movie starring Akshay Kumar can be started right away. And then I saw this…
Stop being polite and formal to everybody around you! This is one of the things I regret most about my character and personality. I try to respect everybody’s decisions, judgements and opinions by being polite to them. I only have formal conversations with people who aren’t my close friends. And as a result my acquaintances remain as acquaintances and I never became close with them. All my life I was taught to be good and friendly to everybody else. Now that is not bad, but I misunderstood that as being polite and formal to everybody around me. I have realised that being polite and formal will actually keep you at a distance from people you want to be friends with. And the relationship you maintain will only be formal and will not be fun. Of course being the “good guy” has its own perks, you’re easily entrusted upon by your peers as they know you will always be there to help when required. People treat you well, with respect and admiration. But you will always feel that emptiness, as there will always be a gap, and you won’t feel completely connected to the other person. This is one thing I want to change about my personality. I want to have more informal and fun conversations with people. I don’t want to be as uptight and proper as I usually am. And I think this will lead to better friendships and better memories.
OUCH. The thing I kept deeply buried within my heart. HOW DID THIS HUMAN FIND WHAT I HAVE BEEN HIDING FOR SO LONG? This was (and still is) a part of my character throughout my life. Then another thing I kept within resurfaced- that almost 99% of my friendships never last after we have no reasons to be around together every day. I’m just not a “fun” person to be around; I don’t “light up” the moment. Being a silent, friend occasionally offering to do/ say things that the others (that do everything else) can easily do is not just enough to be a fun person. And there it was. All the bad thoughts rushed in: reasons for why I could never be a useful person, or how I have always managed to dodge responsibilities, or moments when people actually tried to get help from me and how I unintentionally (sometimes intentionally) denied it was explained to me again, like I was not there to experience it first-hand. One thing that I always knew that I need to change myself, but I don’t want to. I just cannot fathom the amount of confusion and attention I would get for it. The mere thought of people talking about the reasons for my change (if I could make one) was haunting. I just don’t want it to be a thing, you know. I was never a strong person to face confrontations. I couldn’t even talk back to that terrible Uber driver who began to shout at me for giving a bad review. And then I felt sad and had a 3 hour nap. This is not a life-changing encounter for me. It is just a reminder how shit I am being an adult, making my own decisions. Besides, if you still thought I'm probably going to change my habits over a pretentious answer on Quora, then seriously dude, know what you've signed up for (me). etbjnee.

item.title: OH LORDY!
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
Just because I didn't write anything here for months, it doesn't mean that I had a nice social life.

I was not having a nice time either, there's some people in a building that I paid, to show me how much of a bitch college would be. You know..

It was pretty much the same, typing, typing, typin....

and some reports,

and another report,

and some more assignments,

And all those works led to hear this one phrase from those teachers:

"This is not enough."

-It was pretty hard for me, alright? Before this the most I spent with my computer was a 12 hour binge session of FRIENDS and to think that I beat that record by writing a report on "Automated Guided Vehicles Used in Industries Around the World" makes me feel quite sad.

Then again, I took this shit upon myself, so I'm the one to be blamed. 

Speaking of writing about shit, I have a check-list about the thinks that I could possibly write here, and one of them was this:

And I was like, "Well, whats fun about that? I don't even have to try being funny about that, I'll just report what they say right away!

That's right, let's talk politics!

Seriously man, right from our "Bigly Smart Man From The West" to our "Dead Chief Minister's Rule" everything is funny, and nothing is sad.

Let's not talk about the brainy methods of saving water from heat and the dumbasses that supported it, because a lot more dumber shit happened after that. WILD! Right?

I mean, if playing golf and naming other country's capital is what politics is all about, THEN GOD, SIGN ME UP FOR THAT! (Or better make me an actor and they'll vote for me)

To think about it, all these dumbasses on power have come to their position using either of these three things: race, religion or reputation. In the case of the Stable-Genius-In-chief from the west, it's all the three.

Now this is a slippery slope. If you respond to their crap, some people who are unaware of them will learn about them. If you don't, they'll continue to talk shit, and get famous anyway. Then how would you explain an asshole who lost a very small election  in the most pathetic way possible and still make it into headlines?

I know! Lynch churches, file fake cases that those churches are built at government lands, while spending money from temples BUILT ON ROADS on that lawsuit! The world will LOVE YOU!

Make a plan for a bridge that is really great, and make it like you need to take lands from big store owners in that process. Then bargain with them, get money, change the plan, make an absolutely useless construction and WIN! That's politics 101!

And don't forget, threaten and/or kill anyone who questions you.

item.title: why u postpone
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded: i know i am right. I wanted it. I wanted to do it. I really did. If I ever do it, I wanted it to be at that place. It was the one of the best in it. But I couldn't to it, so I settled with a similar, but mediocre place. But, I got a second chance, to do the second step of what I wanted to do, in the exact same place I wanted. I was ecstatic. Every aspect of it.     And still, I have to do those tasks, Just for them to be thrown away that it isn't good enough. I am advised to work harder, work more, work fast That I have to stay encouraged, despite of the negativity. Do all those goddamned tasks, while being told that it isn't going to help my future. That I have to work for more opportunities, despite of denial of permission from the same people. That I wouldn't be told to learn that one particular thing that they'd use to test me with. item.title: masculinity
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
Man, what a word. What does it mean? Lets ask the traditional Dictionary:

It is a beautiful measure of a man’s credibility. But now it basically means, “How much of an asshole you are in this world.” WHAT? HOW COULD YOU SAY THAT? well, lets ask about that to the Urban Dictionary:

Whoa. What is THIS masculinity, anyway?

It is the pretentiousness (ha!) by saying that being single is the best thing, and that women make life worse.

It is the idea of rejecting any healthy expression of one’s emotions, and blaming it on the society that that is what expected on a man. Then sharing memes that says “Men are selfless uwuuu.” It is the ability to reject people like Terry Crews (Who in my opinion is the epitome of REAL masculinity), for doing the right thing.

It is the entitlement a man has on a woman’s modesty. A girl is not good if she doesn’t wear her dupatta.

It is the ability to consider oneself “Friend-Zoned” and complain about it that girls exist in this world only to use them. According to a “nice” guy, being a good friend with a girl for a prolonged period of time automatically gives him a right to be romantic companion to her, and he has total control over her.

It is, like 99.99% of those movies say, that if you disturb a girl every day to the point of exhaustion, she will fall in love with you. (Basically, no means yes)

It is making, liking and sharing memes that degrades women in every way possible to elevate their own kind, with the screenshots of movies they pirated. Oftentimes it is meant to be “touching” by giving advises to girls, but in reality is almost funny and, cringe worthy.

It means being a shitty person by trying to find fault on the victim. Examples:

“It’s because of that leggings she was wearing.”

“It wouldn't have happened if she didn’t go to that street in the middle of the night.”

“Why would she go there? She knows there are goons there. She probably wanted that.”

"This horrible thing happened to her only because she ignored her culture. This would never have happened if she stayed inside her home cutting onions"
 

Nobody is born with these qualities, right? And yeah, this is a character that a kid learns from the circumstances during his growth. Example: “Boys don’t like pink”, “Boys never cry” (You know, almost all of us have used that “Crying like a girl” insult), among a lot others.

A big part in a man’s (toxic) masculinity is ironically, from a woman, the mother. To her, her son is the most innocent person in the world, and he wouldn’t do any harm. She would go lengths defending her son, even from a very young age. Mom fights with the teacher at school for taking disciplinary actions, and this gives the son an idea that being naughty is what every boy does.

Little things like these creates an idea on the mind, and voila! This incredible trait is born!

And whenever conversations about women’s issues comes up, a group saying #NotAllMen arises. OH really. But these (NotAll)men, never try change those (some)men. Instead, they resort to victim blaming. Even when some (NotAll)men actually try to help, they are given a new name, a WhiteKnight.

To these people, all the women who scratched and clawed throughout their life, ignoring all the catcalling, unwanted advances, notorious plots and downright abuse and finally succeed, IS the proof that equality exists.

Here's the funniest part: Men say women act impulsively, and it is a "women thing" to watch local TV series, while they are creating armies and editing the Wikipedia pages of the people they like and hate. Apparently, there was a girl in BIG BOSS who was soo trashy, so these gentlemen edited her Wiki page with terrible words. Such gentle.

If you don't want an entire kind to be blamed for the mistakes for a few, then try not to take pride in being one of that kind. Acknowledge the bad things in it, and try to change them.

  etbjnee

item.title: Welcome to the Gutenberg Editor
item.dc:creator: actualjoe
item.content:encoded:
Of Mountains & Printing Presses

The goal of this new editor is to make adding rich content to WordPress simple and enjoyable. This whole post is composed of pieces of content—somewhat similar to LEGO bricks—that you can move around and interact with. Move your cursor around and you’ll notice the different blocks light up with outlines and arrows. Press the arrows to reposition blocks quickly, without fearing about losing things in the process of copying and pasting.

What you are reading now is a text block the most basic block of all. The text block has its own controls to be moved freely around the post...

... like this one, which is right aligned.

Headings are separate blocks as well, which helps with the outline and organization of your content.

A Picture is Worth a Thousand Words

Handling images and media with the utmost care is a primary focus of the new editor. Hopefully, you’ll find aspects of adding captions or going full-width with your pictures much easier and robust than before.

Try selecting and removing or editing the caption, now you don’t have to be careful about selecting the image or other text by mistake and ruining the presentation.

The Inserter Tool

Imagine everything that WordPress can do is available to you quickly and in the same place on the interface. No need to figure out HTML tags, classes, or remember complicated shortcode syntax. That’s the spirit behind the inserter—the (+) button you’ll see around the editor—which allows you to browse all available content blocks and add them into your post. Plugins and themes are able to register their own, opening up all sort of possibilities for rich editing and publishing.

Go give it a try, you may discover things WordPress can already add into your posts that you didn’t know about. Here’s a short list of what you can currently find there:

  • Text & Headings
  • Images & Videos
  • Galleries
  • Embeds, like YouTube, Tweets, or other WordPress posts.
  • Layout blocks, like Buttons, Hero Images, Separators, etc.
  • And Lists like this one of course :)

Visual Editing

A huge benefit of blocks is that you can edit them in place and manipulate your content directly. Instead of having fields for editing things like the source of a quote, or the text of a button, you can directly change the content. Try editing the following quote:

The editor will endeavor to create a new page and post building experience that makes writing rich posts effortless, and has “blocks” to make it easy what today might take shortcodes, custom HTML, or “mystery meat” embed discovery.

Matt Mullenweg, 2017

The information corresponding to the source of the quote is a separate text field, similar to captions under images, so the structure of the quote is protected even if you select, modify, or remove the source. It’s always easy to add it back.

Blocks can be anything you need. For instance, you may want to add a subdued quote as part of the composition of your text, or you may prefer to display a giant stylized one. All of these options are available in the inserter.

You can change the amount of columns in your galleries by dragging a slider in the block inspector in the sidebar.

Media Rich

If you combine the new wide and full-wide alignments with galleries, you can create a very media rich layout, very quickly:

Sure, the full-wide image can be pretty big. But sometimes the image is worth it.

The above is a gallery with just two images. It’s an easier way to create visually appealing layouts, without having to deal with floats. You can also easily convert the gallery back to individual images again, by using the block switcher.

Any block can opt into these alignments. The embed block has them also, and is responsive out of the box:

You can build any block you like, static or dynamic, decorative or plain. Here’s a pullquote block:

If you want to learn more about how to build additional blocks, or if you are interested in helping with the project, head over to the GitHub repository.

Help build Gutenberg

Thanks for testing Gutenberg!
